venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/public/chair:
US-VOTE: On 28 February 2019 the United States submitted S/2019/186. It received nine votes in favour, three against and three abstentions. China and the Russian Federation voted against it as permanent members, and the draft was not adopted. [US-VOTE]
RU-VOTE: S/2019/190 was a separate Russian draft. It received four votes in favour, seven against and four abstentions and failed to reach the required number of affirmative votes. [RU-VOTE]
The U.S. proposal emphasized peaceful elections under international observation, whereas the Russian draft prioritized inclusive national dialogue via the Montevideo Mechanism. Election observation was central to the U.S. approach, while the Russian text utilized the named dialogue mechanism. The U.S. draft called for unhindered humanitarian access consistent with principles, contrasting with the Russian draft which placed the Government in the lead and required its consent. Available national statements are absent. Neither draft conferred authority. Analytical suggestion: The divergence between international observation and government-led consent highlights deep political fractures. [US-VOTE][RU-VOTE][US-TEXT][RU-TEXT]
venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/CHAIR/chair: S/2019/186 received nine votes in favour, three against, and three abstentions; China and the Russian Federation voted against it as permanent members, and the draft was not adopted [US-VOTE]. S/2019/190 received four votes in favour, seven against, and four abstentions and failed to reach the required number of affirmative votes [RU-VOTE]. The U.S. proposal emphasized peaceful elections under international observation while the Russian draft prioritized inclusive national dialogue including the Montevideo Mechanism, with Equatorial Guinea's Ndong Mba announcing results as Council President noting Equatorial Guinea abstained on S/2019/186 and voted for S/2019/190 [CHAIR]. The U.S. draft proposed unhindered humanitarian access consistent with principles whereas the Russian draft placed Venezuela's Government in the lead requiring its consent. National statements are absent for both drafts. Neither draft conferred authority. Suggestion: Future resolutions must balance electoral mandates with sovereign consent to ensure adoption [US-VOTE, RU-VOTE].
